title: AWS Budgets: alerts before you overspend

kcs.statement: AWS Budgets tracks custom cost budgets, usage budgets, and Reserved Instance or Savings Plans utilization and coverage budgets against thresholds you set.
AWS Budgets sends alerts by email or SNS when actual or forecasted spend crosses a threshold, unlike a CloudWatch billing alarm, which fires only on actual estimated charges.
Budget actions can respond automatically to a breached budget by applying an IAM policy or SCP, or by stopping specific EC2 or RDS instances.

problem_ideas: A startup wants an email when the month is forecast to exceed $500, before it actually does: Budgets or a billing alarm?
A sandbox account must automatically stop its EC2 instances at $200 of spend: which feature?
A company bought RIs and wants an alert if utilization drops below 80%: which budget type?
A billing alarm and a budget are both set at $1,000: which one can fire on the 10th of the month while spend is $400?
Route budget alerts to a Slack channel: which messaging service sits in between?
Spot the false statement: 'AWS Budgets shows a 12-month cost history chart by service.'
